title: Finite-degree descent of an ideal from a space blowup
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Open and closed immersions mean representable morphisms whose scheme base changes have the indicated property [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme; it is quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Morphism properties use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. For a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ on the small etale site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], write $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}T$ for the relative Proj of $\bigoplus_{d\geq0}\mathcal K^d$, constructed by etale descent of the ordinary scheme blowups [def-nagata-global-blowup] on affine etale charts. Finite type means locally generated by finitely many sections. Let $T$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space, let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal, and put $p:T_1=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}T\to T$. For every finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_{T_1}$ there exist an integer $d>0$ and a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal I^d\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ such that, writing $\mathcal E=\operatorname{im}(p^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_{T_1})$, one has the equality of ideal subsheaves on $T_1$ $$\operatorname{im}(p^*\mathcal H\to\mathcal O_{T_1})=\mathcal E^d\mathcal J.$$ No reducedness or density assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal I^n$. Each power is quasi-coherent: it is the image of the multiplication from a tensor product of quasi-coherent modules, computed on affine charts by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus]. Their direct sum is quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits]. By [lem-sfb-space-blowup-chart-properties], $p:P_T(\mathcal A)=T_1\to T$ is proper, in particular quasi-compact (proper includes finite type, which includes quasi-compactness in the stated morphism conventions). The ideal correspondence [lem-sfb-space-ideal-closed-subspace-correspondence] gives the closed subspace $i:Z=V(\mathcal J)\hookrightarrow T_1$ with ideal exactly $\mathcal J$. Since $\mathcal J$ is of finite type, [lem-sfb-space-closed-structure-finite-presentation] makes $i$ of finite presentation.

Apply [lem-sfb-space-proj-finite-degree-equations] to the qcqs base $T$, the graded algebra $\mathcal A$, the quasi-compact $p$, and the finite-presentation closed immersion $i$. Obtain $d>0$ and a finite-type quasi-coherent submodule $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal A_d=\mathcal I^d$ with $Z=P_T(\mathcal A/(\mathcal F\mathcal A))$ as a closed subspace of $T_1$. Regard the composite inclusion $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal I^d\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ as the ideal $\mathcal H$: stability under multiplication by local functions is exactly the submodule condition. It has the same underlying module as $\mathcal F$, hence is quasi-coherent and of finite type. It remains to prove the asserted ideal equality for this $\mathcal H$.

source.place: Tag 085M (lemma-closed-subscheme-proj-finite); Tag 0860, first and second paragraphs.

proof.text: Take any affine etale chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to T$. Write $I=\mathcal I(U)$ and $M=\mathcal H(U)\subseteq I^d$. The affine-chart calculus [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus] identifies the restricted quotient algebra with $B/(MB)$, where $B=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n$ and $M$ is placed in degree $d$. By the scheme-test comparisons [lem-sfb-space-relative-proj-scheme-tests] and the affine-chart clause of [lem-sfb-space-relative-proj-quotient-closed-immersion], the equality from step 2 restricts to $Z_U=\operatorname{Proj}(B/(MB))$ inside $\operatorname{Proj}(B)$, embedded by the closed immersion induced by the quotient map $\psi:B\to B/(MB)$. By [lem-sfb-space-blowup-chart-properties] the latter is covered by $V_a=\operatorname{Spec}C_a$, $C_a=R[I/a]$, for $a\in I$. Write $f=at\in B_1$, where $t$ only records degree. By [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open] this is $D_+(f)$ with coordinate ring $B_{(f),0}$, and the map $\theta_a(xt^n/f^n)=x/a^n$ of [def-nagata-homogeneous-away-to-chart] identifies $B_{(f),0}$ with $C_a$ over $R$ [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart]; below we write $b/f^n$ and its image in $C_a$ interchangeably. Since $B$ is generated by $B_1$ over $B_0=R$, [lem-sfb-graded-proj-quotient-twist-comparison] gives $Z_U\cap D_+(f)=D_+(\psi(f))$, embedded by the surjection $B_{(f),0}\to(B/(MB))_{(\bar f),0}$, $b/f^n\mapsto\bar b/\bar f^n$. The ideal $J_a$ of $Z_U\cap V_a$ is the restriction of $\mathcal J$, by the base-change clause of [lem-sfb-space-ideal-closed-subspace-correspondence].

Compute the ideal of the quotient Proj on this standard open. By step 3 the chart of $Z_U$ is cut out by the kernel of the surjection $B_{(f),0}\to(B/(MB))_{(\bar f),0}$ of [lem-sfb-graded-proj-quotient-twist-comparison]; surjectivity is also seen from the homogeneous-localization description [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero] by lifting homogeneous numerators. Its kernel consists of $b/f^n$ with $b\in B_n$ for which $f^k b\in MB$ for some $k\geq0$, by the defining equality relation for fractions in the quotient. Increase $k$ until $n+k\geq d$. Since $MB$ is generated in degree $d$, write the homogeneous element $f^k b=\sum_j m_j c_j$ with $m_j\in M\subset B_d$ and $c_j\in B_{n+k-d}$. Then $$b/f^n=\sum_j(m_j/f^d)(c_j/f^{n+k-d}).$$ Conversely every $m/f^d$ maps to zero. Thus, as an ideal and not just a zero set, $J_a=(m/a^d:m\in M)\subset C_a$. This argument is valid also when $f$ is nilpotent and both localized rings are zero.

source.place: Tag 0860 (lemma-composition-finite-type-blowups), last paragraph: meaning of the homogeneous equations on the affine blowup chart.

proof.text: On $C_a=R[I/a]$ one has $IC_a=(a)$: for $x\in I$, $x=a(x/a)$, while $a\in I$. For $m\in M\subseteq I^d$, the element $m/a^d$ belongs to $C_a$, since $I^d$ is generated by products of $d$ elements of $I$. The image of $m$ in $C_a$ is exactly $a^d(m/a^d)$. Consequently $$MC_a=(a^d)J_a=(IC_a)^dJ_a.$$ The tensor-pullback definition [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] identifies the image of $p^*\mathcal H$ on this chart with $MC_a$, and the image of $p^*\mathcal I$ with $IC_a$: the multiplication map sends $c\otimes m$ to $cm$. These formulas also identify products with their ordinary chart ideals. Hence the desired equality holds on every $V_a$ of every affine etale $U\to T$. These charts cover $T_1$ by step 3, so equality holds as ideal subsheaves: membership in a subsheaf is local and the two local inclusions give both global inclusions. No cancellation in $R$, reducedness, or density is used.
